Problem Description

You are building a text analyzer tool. One of its features is detecting vowel clusters in a word.

Your task is to write a program that takes a word and counts how many vowel clusters it contains.

What is a Vowel Cluster?

A vowel cluster is a group of one or more vowels (a, e, i, o, u) that appear consecutively without any consonants in between.

Examples:

- "ae" is one vowel cluster.  
- "a" is one vowel cluster.  
- "abc" has one vowel cluster: "a".  

For example, in the word "beautiful", the vowels "eau" form one vowel cluster. Later, "i" and "u" form their own clusters. Hence, the word contains 3 vowel clusters in total.

An iterative method, called the Babylonian method, for finding square roots, was known to the ancient Babylonians (1500 BC) and Greeks (100 AD) long before Newton invented his general procedure. Here's how it works. Suppose you are given any positive number S. To find the square root of S, do the following: Make an initial guess. Guess any positive number x0.Improve the guess. Problem Description

A robber is planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money. However, the robber cannot rob two adjacent houses because doing so will trigger the alarm system.

Your task is to determine the maximum amount of money the robber can steal without robbing two adjacent houses.

You must solve this problem using recursion and/or memoization.

Output Format
